strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing elastic inference across heterogeneous hardware with clear practical relevance
Novel insight that progressive capacity expansion (not just depth) is necessary for vision tasks, validated empirically via Table 1
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple ImageNet variants, extensive ablations (Tables 6-7), and strong baselines comparison
Solid technical execution with token recycling mechanism and entropy-based routing that is simple yet effective
Good presentation with clear figures, thorough appendices supporting reproducibility, and plug-in compatibility with vanilla ViTs
Consistent improvements over nested baselines: up to 2.0 p.p. at equal throughput and 2.9 p.p. at equal GMACs
weaknesses: Fundamental limitation on uniformly difficult datasets (Section 4.5): performance gains critically diminish on ImageNet-A where most inputs require second-stage inference, undermining efficiency benefits in harder deployment scenarios

Strict restriction to vanilla ViT architecture limits practical applicability; no evaluation on hierarchical transformers (Swin, MambaVision) which are increasingly prevalent, despite claims they only 'complicate' slicing

Routing mechanism insufficiently justified: Shannon entropy is simple; claim of parity with complex criteria not empirically validated; entropy thresholds appear manually tuned; negative learned α value (-0.19) unexplained
Training efficiency not quantified: Section 3.3 acknowledges computational intensity but provides no concrete overhead measurements—critical practical information is missing
Limited depth scaling: Table 3 shows 3-stage variants yield diminishing returns with high computational cost, suggesting poor scalability for deeper hierarchies
Evaluation scope restricted to ImageNet classification; no transfer tasks, actual hardware latency/memory measurements, or non-ViT architectures tested
Early exit comparison uses mismatched depths (24 vs 12 layers); parameter-count not controlled across all baseline comparisons; sensitivity to DeiT-Tiny initialization unclear

strengths: Well-motivated problem of elastic inference for ViTs with practical relevance to heterogeneous deployment
Table 1 provides principled justification for why progressive expansion is necessary in vision (unlike LLMs), distinguishing the approach
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple nested baselines, ImageNet variants, and thorough ablations of recycling/fusion strategies
Honest and transparent discussion of limitations (Section 4.5, Appendix J), particularly the acknowledged failure mode on uniformly difficult inputs
Practical design as plugin-compatible upgrade for vanilla ViTs without parameter duplication vs. ensemble-based routing
Insightful visualizations of entropy distributions (Figures 5-6) and load distribution analysis (Figure 8) supporting the routing mechanism
weaknesses: Incremental improvements (2.0-2.9pp) are modest for a novel method; marginal benefit over DeiT-Small baseline (79.9%) is unclear for practitioners

Critical limitation on uniformly difficult inputs: ImageNet-A performance degrades to 73.6% with 3H subset (Figure 7), negating early-exit benefits and severely restricting real-world applicability (medical imaging, fine-grained classification often have inherently difficult inputs)

Extremely narrow evaluation scope: single domain (ImageNet classification only), single model scale (DeiT-Tiny primary), no detection/segmentation/multimodal tasks; generalization to ViT-Base and larger models undemonstrated

Incomplete technical justification: (1) learned α converges to negative values (-0.19 in Table 7) suggesting model subtracts rather than builds upon prior embeddings—counterintuitive and unexplained; (2) entropy routing justified only by performing 'on par' with alternatives, without rigorous ablation or principled threshold selection

Unfair comparisons: Table 1 baselines undertrained without joint training strategy; Appendix B Early Exit uses 24 layers vs. ThinkingViT's 12; parameter count increase (5.7M→22.1M) underemphasized despite being 3.9× overhead

Configuration and hyperparameter sensitivity: 3H→6H selected from many options with ~100 training runs; large accuracy variations across loss weights (λ) in Table 2 raise concerns about selection bias and reproducibility without clear principled criteria

Limited novelty: nested slicing from prior work (HydraViT, SortedNet), progressive head activation is straightforward scaling, token recycling is a simple learned scalar blend, entropy routing is established early-stopping—core contribution is primarily combining existing techniques

Missing critical analyses: no explanation of negative recycling mechanism; no memory/caching overhead analysis; no hardware latency measurements (only A100 throughput); unclear how to select hyperparameters (thresholds, λ values, expansion ratios) for new datasets

Narrow experimental scope fails breadth requirements: no cross-domain evaluation (COCO, ADE20K), no larger model scales (ViT-Base), no combination studies with other efficiency techniques (pruning, quantization), no edge device deployment

Reproducibility concerns: extensive hyperparameter sensitivity without principled selection; different configurations show large variance; implementation details underspecified (Proj_{d_i→d_j} never fully defined); no code availability mentioned

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical value: addresses genuine inefficiency of fixed compute allocation in nested Transformers
Clever Token Recycling mechanism effectively justified by Table 1, demonstrating why naive iteration fails for vision unlike LLMs

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple SOTA baselines, evaluation across 6 ImageNet variants, thorough ablations (Tables 2-7), detailed analysis of prediction dynamics and entropy distributions
Strong empirical results achieving 81.44% accuracy with 22.1M parameters (outperforming DeiT-Small at 79.9%), with demonstrated scalability to 3-stage variants
Practical design with real-world applicability: backbone-preserving architecture, elastic inference via threshold tuning, compatibility with token pruning/patch merging methods
Honest and transparent discussion of limitations, particularly reduced effectiveness on uniformly hard datasets (ImageNet-A/R), demonstrating methodological rigor
Clear presentation with informative figures (especially Figure 6 validating entropy-based routing) and well-structured methodology sections
weaknesses: Incremental novelty combining existing techniques: nested Transformers (MatFormer, HydraViT), early stopping via confidence, and feature fusion are all well-established; contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation

Experimental setup fairness concerns: all baselines initialized from DeiT-Tiny (may bias toward ThinkingViT design), unclear if baselines receive equal tuning despite ~100 training runs mentioned, no comparison with alternative thinking-based methods (Guo et al. 2025, Shao et al. 2024)

Shallow analysis of entropy-based routing: claims to match complex criteria (Jitkrittum et al. 2023) but provides no empirical validation against alternative routing mechanisms (Kag et al. 2023, Ding et al. 2025); Shannon entropy is crude proxy for input difficulty

Fundamental dataset-dependent limitation: performance advantage drops substantially on ImageNet-A/R when most inputs are difficult, suggesting method effectiveness is highly sensitive to input distribution, reducing generalizability
Parameter efficiency concerns inadequately addressed: 22.1M parameters vs. DeiT-Tiny's 5.7M is 4× overhead; while acknowledged, thorough cost-benefit analysis relative to gains is missing

Limited evaluation scope: single domain (ImageNet classification only), no edge device deployment testing (only A100 measurements), no evaluation on detection/segmentation tasks, entropy computation overhead not analyzed
Entropy threshold selection lacks principled guidance: Table 4 shows results across thresholds but provides no systematic methodology for selecting τ for specific deployment scenarios
Statistical rigor absent: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple seeds reported; improvements often 0.3-1.0% potentially within noise; single-seed results may be unreliable

Token Recycling design justification incomplete: simple linear projection (Eq. 3) compared to alternatives only with non-optimal training (stochastic instead of joint in Table 6); no exploration of learnable composition or attention-based fusion
Overthinking phenomenon (2% round-1-correct but round-2-wrong in Figure 9) under-explored; negative learned α=-0.19 not explained; no analysis of whether effect is class or input-property specific

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Elastic inference across heterogeneous hardware is practically important and clearly articulated

Elegant routing mechanism: Using prediction entropy as global-image-level signal avoids expensive MLP-based routers; the argument that token-level routers cannot capture image-level difficulty is well-justified

Comprehensive experimental validation: Comparisons with strong baselines (MatFormer, HydraViT, SortedNet, DynaBERT), robustness on ImageNet variants (V2, Real, R, A, Sketch), extensions to semantic segmentation (ADE20K, Cityscapes), and hierarchical architectures (Swin)

Token Recycling insight: Observation that naive recursive inference plateaus (Table 1) motivates progressive capacity expansion; ablations convincingly show Final-Layer Token Recycling outperforms alternatives
Strong empirical results: Consistent 2.0 p.p. improvements at equal throughput and 2.9 p.p. at equal GMACs across multiple datasets and settings
Excellent visualizations and analysis: Figures 5-7 effectively show entropy-based routing behavior and load distributions; supplementary material thoroughly documents design choices and failure cases
Backbone-compatible design: Enables seamless transfer to downstream tasks without retraining, demonstrating practical applicability
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with effective diagrams, intuitive explanations, and comprehensive supplementary material
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Individual components (nested networks, entropy-based early stopping, learnable token projection) are well-established; main contribution is combining existing ideas, which feels incremental

Insufficient mechanistic analysis: Paper shows width expansion outperforms depth expansion empirically (Figure 8b) but lacks deeper insight into why this occurs in vision tasks; Table 1 (naive iteration plateau) only shown for DeiT-Tiny

Token Recycling justification gaps: Learned α converges to −0.19 with no conceptual explanation for negative weighting; KV-cache variant (Table 4) dramatically underperforms (75.67% vs 80.05%) without analysis; why learnable projection outperforms padding (Table 5) unexplained

Fairness of baseline comparisons: All baselines use static compute allocation; no comparison against input-adaptive variants of existing methods; 3H→6H configuration appears tuned to ImageNet-1K (Figure 3), generalization unclear

Training cost and overhead not quantified: Appendix I acknowledges higher training costs for nested models but provides no memory/time benchmarks; ~100 training runs mentioned raises selection bias concerns (cherry-picking risk); Token Recycling overhead (projection + entropy computation) magnitude unknown

Hyperparameter sensitivity under-explored: Entropy threshold τ selection strategy at deployment time not discussed; 3H→6H vs 3H→9H vs 3H→12H trade-offs are dataset-dependent without principled selection guidance; loss weighting [0.5, 0.5] not optimized relative to alternatives

Batch inference efficiency concerns: Algorithm 1 shows dynamic batch shrinkage causing potential GPU underutilization; no empirical analysis of latency overhead from dynamic batching; GMACs/throughput measured at batch size 512 may not reflect real-world small-batch performance

Generalization and scalability questions: Most experiments focus on ImageNet-1K domain; Swin extension uses hand-crafted allocation (entire stage 1 + half of stages 2-4) not generalizable to other hierarchical architectures; no results on larger models (ViT-L/H); extreme pruning regimes (1H→2H) unexplored

Overthinking failure mode unaddressed: ~2% of samples correct in round 1 become misclassified in round 2 (Figure 13); attributed to overthinking but no proposed solution (confidence calibration, ensemble voting) provided; erodes practical trust

Incomplete statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; unclear if 2-2.9 p.p. improvements are statistically significant given training variance; single runs on downstream tasks (segmentation, Swin) without variance quantification

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple ImageNet variants, hierarchical architectures (Swin), and downstream tasks (semantic segmentation)
Practical design that avoids separate routing networks, using simple entropy-based confidence for early stopping
Solid empirical results with consistent 2.0-2.9 p.p. improvements across benchmarks
Well-written presentation with effective figures (especially Figures 2 and 5) illustrating the approach
Extensive ablation studies in appendix examining token recycling, fusion strategies, and architecture configurations
Demonstrates generalizability beyond vanilla ViT to other architectures and tasks
weaknesses: Limited novelty: combines well-established techniques (nested networks, confidence-based early stopping, embedding fusion) without significant conceptual advance—for CVPR, the bar should be higher for such incremental combinations

Experimental fairness concerns: unclear if baseline methods received the same weighted multi-stage joint training (Eq. 5) as ThinkingViT; if not, improvements conflate multi-stage training benefits with progressive expansion benefits
Marginal performance improvements: 2 p.p. gains are meaningful but not exceptional; without deeper mechanistic insights, such incremental improvements are insufficient for acceptance at a top venue

Weak justification for progressive expansion: Table 1 (naive iteration) only tests one model and may reflect poor optimization rather than fundamental limitation; paper lacks explanation of what representational capacity is gained by expanding from 3H to 6H

Arbitrary and sensitive design choices: 3H→6H configuration selected pragmatically without principled justification; Appendix I admits performance suffers when jumping too far (3H→12H vs. 3H→9H), indicating high sensitivity; learned fusion weight α converges to counterintuitive negative value (-0.19) without explanation

Insufficient mechanistic analysis: Token recycling strategy comparison (Table 4) and fusion strategy comparison (Table 5) show empirical winners but provide limited insight into why; entropy-based routing claimed to match complex criteria but not validated empirically on ViTs

Training overhead not rigorously analyzed: joint multi-stage training is more expensive than single-model training; no wall-clock comparison provided; acknowledged in Appendix I but dismissed without proper analysis
Routing overhead not quantified: entropy computation, re-batching, and pipeline synchronization have non-zero costs on GPUs; no end-to-end throughput analysis with these overheads
Lack of statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, error bars, or reported number of random seeds; with ~100 training runs mentioned, variance analysis would strengthen claims
Limited downstream evaluation: semantic segmentation only on Segmenter architecture; generalization to other methods/tasks not demonstrated

strengths: Well-motivated solution to practical elastic inference problem with clear insight (Table 1) that naive iteration fails for vision models, motivating progressive expansion strategy

Comprehensive and convincing experimental validation: 2.0-2.9 p.p. improvements across multiple settings, robust evaluation on ImageNet variants (V2, Real, R), extension to semantic segmentation and Swin Transformer
Thoughtful design with Token Recycling mechanism (Eq. 4) that elegantly fuses embeddings; entropy-based routing avoids separate routing networks and is interpretable

Exceptional ablation studies: Table 3 provides detailed trade-off curves across thresholds; Figure 3 systematically evaluates configurations; Tables 4-5 compare recycling/fusion strategies; Figure 6 shows insightful entropy distributions

Practical applicability: backbone-preserving design enables seamless integration as drop-in replacement; compatible with token-level pruning; clean algorithmic description (Algorithm 1) for batched inference
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 2, 5) that communicate mechanism and adaptive behavior; well-organized main paper with comprehensive supplementary material
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: nested models, attention slicing, and early stopping are well-established; primary contribution is combining progressive width expansion with entropy routing—a sensible but incremental combination

Insufficient analysis of why progressive expansion works: Table 1 shows naive iteration fails but lacks mechanistic explanation; no analysis of why width expansion outperforms depth-based early exit (Section 4.7); no theoretical justification

Training fairness concern: ThinkingViT uses joint training (Eq. 5) while baselines use standard recipes [41], making attribution of improvements unclear (architecture vs. training procedure); no ablation with identical training for baselines

Entropy threshold τ requires manual tuning for each deployment scenario; while enabling elastic inference, no principled method for setting τ given hardware constraints; less elegant than hardware-agnostic solutions

Incomplete failure mode analysis: ~16% of samples misclassified in both rounds (Figure 13) with no characterization of failure cases or investigation of fixes; missed opportunity for insights into fundamental limitations

Token Recycling design choices underexplored: learnable scalar α is crude; negative α value (-0.19) unexplained and counterintuitive; empirical-only justification for final-layer recycling superiority over alternatives

Limited experimental scope: concentrated on ImageNet classification and segmentation; no evaluation on detection, instance segmentation, or other domains; primarily DeiT-Tiny backbone (Swin extension limited)
Throughput measurements on A100 with batch size 512 may not transfer to realistic deployments with smaller batches; no analysis of how batch size affects efficiency gains on edge devices
Reproducibility gaps: code availability not mentioned; some hyperparameter choices (loss weights λᵢ, α initialization) lack thorough justification; would benefit from public release
